uncited: Tile-based Rasterization with Radix Sort is a GPU-parallel rasterization method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that divides the image into tiles to manage memory and processing load, assigning Gaussians to tiles based on their projected 2D splats [Parent].

It solves the performance bottleneck of per-pixel sorting by using a single global radix sort to achieve per-tile depth ordering, enabling real-time performance for millions of splats [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].

Unlike sibling methods that may perform redundant depth sorting or evaluate splats against irrelevant pixels, this method ensures that each tile is processed by one GPU thread block walking a single sorted list [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].

The method operates on a list of $N$ projected 2D Gaussian splats, each defined by center $(x_i, y_i)$, 2D covariance matrix $\Sigma'_i$, color $c_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, and depth $Z_c$ [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
The image is divided into a grid of tiles with dimensions $T_w \times T_h$ (typically $16 \times 16$ pixels) [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
**Tile Assignment:** Each Gaussian is assigned to every tile its projected 2D splat touches.
If a splat straddles tile boundaries, it is duplicated into each relevant tile [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
This creates one work item per (Gaussian, tile) pair [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
**Key Packing:** For each (splat, tile) pair, a 64-bit integer sort key is constructed.
The tile ID is packed into the high bits, and the splat's depth $Z_c$ is packed into the low bits [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
where `tile_id` is the 1D tile index ($y \times \text{grid\_width} + x$) and $Z_c$ is cast to a 32-bit unsigned integer [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
**Global Radix Sort:** A single GPU radix sort is performed over all (splat, tile) pairs [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
This simultaneously bins splats by tile ID (ensuring contiguity) and sorts them by depth within each tile [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
After sorting, each tile is processed by one GPU thread block that walks the sorted list [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].

For each pixel in a tile, front-to-back compositing is performed using the tile's sorted list of splats, evaluating per-pixel alpha $\alpha_i(\mathbf{x})$ and breaking early when transmittance $T < \epsilon$ [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
The same sorted lists are reused for backpropagation, allowing gradients to flow to position, shape, opacity, and color without additional sorting [Sibling: Tile-based Rasteriser].
If `idx == 0`, set `ranges[currtile].x = 0`.
If `idx > 0`, read `prevtile = point_list_keys[idx - 1] >> 32`.
If `currtile != prevtile`, set `ranges[prevtile].y = idx` and `ranges[currtile].x = idx`.
The method builds on [Tiled 2D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization](2061-tiled-2d-gaussian-splatting-rasterization.md).
